account: The node's objective is the analytical product itself: derive reconciliation hypotheses and evaluation-design constraints from separator facts already supplied by the sibling extractors. The separator facts contain all needed findings from Smit et al. and Zhang et al. (e.g., null results, task dependence, model heterogeneity), making further decomposition unnecessary. The acceptance condition is mechanical: at least three reconciliation hypotheses, at least three evaluation-design constraints, each labeled as design inference, covering the five metric families. These can be produced now.

decidability.account: All evidence required for this analytical node is present as separator facts. The node does not need to read the full corpus texts because the relevant findings are already extracted and anchored with page markers. The derivation task is a synthesis exercise, not an evidence-collection one. No future sibling output is required; the two sibling extractors' findings are frozen in the separator facts. The acceptance condition is a checklist (count, labeling, coverage) that can be verified locally.
